steps.explanation: Dividing by the magnitude rescales the vector to length 1 without changing its direction

spec.body_markdown:
## Unit Vectors

A unit vector has magnitude exactly 1 and represents pure direction. Given any nonzero vector v, its unit vector is v̂ = v / |v| - dividing by the magnitude rescales the length to 1 while leaving the direction unchanged.

The standard basis unit vectors î, ĵ, k̂ point along the x, y, and z axes respectively, and any vector can be written as a sum of scaled unit vectors: v = v_xî + v_yĵ + v_z k̂.
